title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Announces Deal with Nine Additional Pharmaceutical Manufacturers to Lower Drug Prices for Americans
key_claim: The White House counts 26 pharmaceutical manufacturers with MFN deals, covering 89% of the branded drug market, after nine more signed on 31 August 2026.
frame_summary: Presents the pricing deals as a contracting success that lowers US drug prices, with the 26-company, 89% coverage figure offered as proof of national pricing leverage, and says nothing about tariffs on the page.
verbatim_quote: The agreements bring the total number of pharmaceutical manufacturers with MFN deals to 26, covering 89% of the branded drug market.
notes: Primary government statement; the page carries no tariff language, so the link to the Section 232 rates is made through the proclamation.

title: CSMS # 69415934 - GUIDANCE: Reduction of Tariffs on Patented Pharmaceuticals and Pharmaceutical Ingredients for Products of the United Kingdom Implemented by Presidential Proclamation 11020
key_claim: The US tariff rate on patented pharmaceuticals and ingredients that are products of the United Kingdom was cut from 10% to 0% effective 31 July 2026.
frame_summary: Treats the UK rate cut as a routine customs implementation of Proclamation 11020, showing that a country's rate moves by notice once an agreement is concluded; the bulletin itself gives no reason for the cut.
verbatim_quote: reducing the tariff rate for patented pharmaceuticals and associated pharmaceutical ingredients that are products of the United Kingdom from 10 percent to 0 percent, effective July 31, 2026
notes: Date is US month-first (1 August 2026). The pricing-agreement link comes from the Forbes piece and the Bureau of Industry and Security notice filed 31 July 2026 (not cited, PDF).

title: Adjusting Imports of Pharmaceuticals and Pharmaceutical Ingredients Into the United States (Proclamation 11020)
key_claim: Proclamation 11020 sets a 100% default duty on patented pharmaceuticals, a 15% rate for Japan, the EU, South Korea and Switzerland jointly, 20% for companies with approved onshoring plans rising to 100% on 2 April 2030, and zero until 20 January 2029 for eligible companies with MFN pricing agreements.
frame_summary: Writes a default 100% duty and then defines the real rate by who the importer or country is: country caps, approved onshoring plans and HHS pricing agreements each lower it on dated terms.
verbatim_quote: The ad valorem duty rate for patented pharmaceuticals and associated pharmaceutical ingredients, as listed in Annex I to this proclamation, shall be 15 percent for products of Japan, the European Union, the Republic of Korea, and Switzerland and Liechtenstein jointly
verbatim_list: Imports of patented pharmaceuticals and associated pharmaceutical ingredients, as listed in Annex I to this proclamation, will be subject to a 100 percent ad valorem duty rate.
The aforementioned 20 percent rate shall increase to 100 percent on April 2, 2030.
the applicable ad valorem tariff rate for pharmaceuticals and associated pharmaceutical ingredients shall be zero until January 20, 2029.
notes: Structural anchor (published 9 April 2026 as 91 FR 18183, filed 8 April, signed 2 April). Quotes verified by fetching the federalregister.gov full-text XML of the same document; the HTML page above carries the publication-date metadata.

title: Tracking MFN's impact on innovative medicine launches: separating the signal from the noise
key_claim: The US accounts for 68% of cumulative first-five-year revenue for innovative medicines and EU4+UK for 16%, and IQVIA judges it too early to attribute the fall in European launches to MFN policy.
frame_summary: Argues that the fall in European launches began before the MFN actions and cannot yet be pinned on them, while showing why the US-versus-Europe revenue split gives companies reason to protect US prices.
verbatim_quote: It is too early to attribute this to MFN policy.
verbatim_list: The US alone accounts for 68%, while the EU4+UK contribute 16%.

Together, the US and the top five European markets — Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the UK — account for 84% of cumulative revenue in the first five years for innovative prescription medicines, defined here as Novel Active Substances (NAS), measured at list price.
notes: Used for the revenue split and as sourced counter-evidence. Data-provider analysis, not peer-reviewed.

title: The Lancet: New US Medicare pricing policies could reshape global pharmaceutical markets, potentially driving up prices and delaying medicine launches worldwide, study suggests
key_claim: A Lancet cohort study finds the lowest benchmark price in the US Medicare reference models is 71% lower than what Medicare pays, and that manufacturers could respond by changing formulations, converting discounts to confidential rebates or delaying launches.
frame_summary: Argues that reference-pricing models give manufacturers a strong incentive to change how they price and launch products outside the US, because for most medicines the US saving exceeds sales in the country used to set the price.
verbatim_quote: Under these payment models, the lowest price used as an international benchmark was found to be 71% lower than what Medicare pays, with South Korea, Norway, and Australia as the most common countries referenced by Medicare to set pricing.
verbatim_list: Manufacturers could try to do that by developing different formulations, converting existing discounts into confidential rebates, or delaying launches.
notes: Press release for the peer-reviewed Lancet paper (DOI 10.1016/S0140-6736(26)01555-2); the Lancet page itself returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool, so the journal release is the verified text. Classified Tier 2 because a press release about Tier 1 research is not itself Tier 1.

title: US Commerce Department defines specialty pharmaceutical categories eligible for zero Section 232 tariff and identifies eligible jurisdictions
date_evidence: 23 Sep 2026 Subject Tax Alerts Categories Customs & Excise taxes Jurisdictions United States
key_claim: The 100% duty applied from 31 July 2026 to the companies in Annex III and from 29 September 2026 to all other companies; 19 jurisdictions are eligible for zero-rate specialty categories on the basis of a trade and security agreement.
frame_summary: Describes Commerce's mechanics for the 29 September cliff: zero-rate specialty categories open to 19 jurisdictions with trade and security agreements, and the full rate for every other company.
verbatim_quote: The 100% ad valorem tariff on covered patented pharmaceutical products and associated ingredients has applied since 31 July 2026 for the companies listed in Annex III of the Proclamation and takes effect 29 September 2026 for all other companies.
verbatim_list: Nineteen jurisdictions are eligible on the basis of a current or forthcoming trade and security framework agreement
notes: Consultancy summary of the Bureau of Industry and Security notice published 23 September 2026.

title: U.S.-U.K. Deal To Raise Drug Prices In Britain Faces Major Challenges
key_claim: The UK agreed to elevate drug prices in exchange for zero tariffs, including a 25% rise in NICE's cost-effectiveness threshold, and the NHS has not budgeted for the extra spending.
frame_summary: Argues that the UK bought its zero tariff with a higher NICE threshold that the NHS has not funded, so the deal's burden falls on health budgets and puts delivery at risk.
verbatim_quote: agreeing to elevate drug prices in exchange for zero tariffs
verbatim_list: a 25% increase to £25,000-37,500/QALY was part of the U.S.-U.K. deal
The NHS hasn't properly budgeted for the increase in spending needed to allow for reimbursement of more pharmaceuticals and keep funding levels for other services and technologies the same.
notes: Contributor column by a health-economics academic; used for the deal terms and budget risk, directionally. The 25% NICE threshold rise is attributed on the page to Politico reporting. The column claim that the UK is the sole European country with such a deal is not used.

title: Interpharma sieht Zugang zu innovativen Medikamenten unter Druck
key_claim: Interpharma says its members did not submit seven of 22 new innovative medicines for reimbursement listing between January 2025 and June 2026 and wants a price-setting system compatible with the US MFN regime.
frame_summary: Reports the Swiss research-pharma association's claim that US reference pricing is already keeping new medicines out of Swiss reimbursement and that Switzerland should adopt a pricing system compatible with the US regime.
verbatim_quote: Zwischen Januar 2025 und Juni 2026 hätten die Mitglieder von Interpharma sieben von insgesamt 22 neuen innovativen Arzneimitteln nicht zur Aufnahme in die Spezialitätenliste eingereicht.
notes: German-language wire report of an industry association's claim (advocacy source, treat directionally). No in-window German-language Tier 1 or Tier 2 source was found: the Swiss Federal Council page on US health topics (bag.admin.ch) is undated with latest entry 29 March 2026, and the Federal Council release of 19 February 2026 is outside the window.
